Campaign brief: Resend gives this engineer a separate sending route for authentication email through familiar developer integrations, with no daily sending limit on paid plans; the Free plan remains limited to 100 emails per day.
events.reader:
Selected audience: The one backend engineer at a ten-person product team who owns email because nobody else does.
Situation context (grounded; check applicability): Individual engineers integrating a hosted auth platform (Supabase Auth) into a product's signup, password-reset, invite, and OTP flows post first-person accounts, in GitHub issues and discussions on the platform's own repos, of hitting the built-in email rate limit and having to reason through Supabase's dashboard logs, SMTP settings, and plan tiers themselves to diagnose it.
events.reader_segment: The one backend engineer at a ten-person product team who owns email because nobody else does
events.promise: Resend gives this engineer a separate sending route for authentication email through familiar developer integrations, with no daily sending limit on paid plans; the Free plan remains limited to 100 emails per day.
events.arc: Move in one email from the recognizable risk of a built-in authentication-email ceiling, to Resend as the separate sending route, to evidence that a contained test can be practical, and then to a free-account CTA.

emails.job: Get a non-customer to create a free Resend account and scope a test of one authentication-email flow before relying on the hosted auth platform’s built-in sender for a launch or signup spike.
emails.single_idea: Resend is the separate email-sending route a small product team can put behind authentication flows when a hosted platform’s built-in sender is no longer an acceptable ceiling; paid Resend plans have no daily sending limit, while Free provides a bounded starting point at 100 emails per day.
emails.objection: Switching email providers sounds like a project this engineer does not have time to take on.
must_not_say: Do not say Resend changes, bypasses, or automatically raises the hosted auth platform’s own rate-limit setting.
Do not promise to detect an upstream SMTP-configuration wipe or explain another platform’s send accounting.
Do not say the Free plan removes daily limits; it is capped at 100 emails per day.
Do not claim transactional messages and marketing Broadcasts are isolated by default or that a dedicated IP is included for this reader.
Do not turn Raycast’s 30-minute waitlist-email test into a claim that a complete migration takes 30 minutes.
Do not lead with security, uptime, dedicated IPs, Automations, Broadcasts, funding, or the full customer roster; they dilute this email’s argument.
Do not imply the recipient has already suffered an outage; frame the rate-limit scenario conditionally.

Resend is a separate provider, not a change to the auth platform's own limiter: the platform's dashboard rate limit still has to be raised by hand after wiring SMTP, and Resend's own free tier reimposes a 100-emails-a-day cap.

Only the paid tiers remove the daily cap; on the free plan the engineer swaps one 100/day ceiling for another, and nothing in the ledger speaks to the auth platform's own rate-limit setting that still has to be raised.
emails.felt_need: Auth email sending (signup confirmation, OTP, magic link, invites) gets blocked with a 429 email rate limit error under normal usage, even when the reporter believes they are under the documented limit.
emails.status_quo: Checks the platform's own Auth logs in the dashboard to verify whether the documented email limit was actually exceeded.
emails.why_it_fails: Upgrading the hosted platform’s subscription does not itself raise the built-in email-provider limit; using a separate SMTP provider and adjusting the platform’s own rate-limit setting are distinct steps.
emails.mechanism: Connect Resend through a supported SDK, REST, or SMTP route. The Free plan is capped at 100 emails per day, while Pro, Scale, and Enterprise have no daily limit.
emails.next_step_decision: Decide whether one authentication-email flow is worth testing through Resend before adopting it more broadly.
emails.next_step_value: Create an account and choose a supported SDK, REST, or SMTP route for a contained first test; Raycast’s documented experience provides evidence that a limited waitlist-email test can be completed quickly without claiming the same duration for this reader.
emails.next_step_limit: This step does not prove production deliverability, complete a full migration, or alter the hosted auth platform’s own rate-limit setting. Getting started still requires a verified domain and Resend API key, and the Free plan remains capped at 100 emails per day.

alternative_arguments.belief_shift: Before: adopting an email platform means fully outsourcing the team’s email program. After: Resend can take on template delivery and revision management while components remain in the team’s code workflow.
must_not_say: Do not claim Resend fully replaces or outsources the reader’s transactional-email program.
Do not promise compatibility with existing components or a specific migration duration.
Do not present template management as a solution to the hosted auth platform’s rate limits.
Do not imply unlimited historical observability; data retention is bounded by plan.
alternative_arguments.objection: I do not want to surrender the email components and application logic we already manage in-house.

alternative_arguments.next_step_value: Review the documented React Email approach and the template-ID-plus-variables sending mechanism.
alternative_arguments.next_step_limit: Reading the documentation does not establish compatibility with the current codebase, migration effort, or production delivery behavior; a verified domain and Resend API key are still required to get started.

events.preview_text: Establish a separate sending route before a launch or signup spike.
events.body:
Route one authentication-email flow through Resend before a launch or signup spike. Resend is a developer email sending platform for transactional messages, with SDK, REST, and SMTP integration paths.

If a hosted auth sender returns a 429, dashboard logs can confirm what happened. But upgrading the platform plan does not itself raise the built-in email-provider limit. Connecting SMTP and adjusting the platform’s rate-limit setting remain separate steps.

The Free plan gives you a bounded place to start at **100 emails per day**. Pro, Scale, and Enterprise plans have **no daily limit**.

Raycast began with a small waitlist-email test and completed it in 30 minutes. That is not a migration estimate, but it shows the value of testing one contained flow before adopting a provider more broadly.

Create an account, verify your domain, and choose the integration route that fits the flow you want to evaluate.

events.subject: Separate template revisions from sending code
events.preview_text: Resend pairs React Email components with published templates, IDs, and variables.
events.body:
Checking Auth logs can explain a rate-limit response. It still leaves template editing, publishing, and revision history to maintain alongside application sending code.

We’re introducing Resend, a developer email sending platform for transactional messages through SDKs, REST, or SMTP. Keep email components in React Email, publish templates, and send them with a template ID and variables.

The editor provides autosave, publishing, and revision history around those templates. This separates template delivery and revision management from the sending call while application logic remains in your code workflow.

The documentation shows the React Email approach and the template-ID-plus-variables mechanism. Use it to decide whether one authentication-email flow is worth scoping as a contained test before a launch or signup spike.

edits.line: Raycast began with a small waitlist-email test and completed it in 30 minutes. That is not a migration estimate, but it shows the value of testing one contained flow before adopting a provider more broadly.

edits.line: Resend is a developer email sending platform for transactional messages, with SDK, REST, and SMTP integration paths.
